about: Hand-off 06 known answers. 'must' rows are acceptance checks; 'info' rows are context. Made by the club's reviewer on 19 Nov 2026 from KPC-Links main 5e84846 with the real code (known-answers/grid_band.py, the Handoff 9 fixture, the key index). Check each against the code before you rely on it.

baseline.handoff9_test: tests/test_fers_handoff9_nov17.py ends ALL PASS (Python 3.13.18, numpy 2.5.3, opencv 5.0.0)
baseline.note: work on a full checkout: without .github/key-rules-version.json the hash reads 5e61f29b2e67, which is wrong

rows.what: the band is one grid cell, read from CELL, not a typed number
rows.expect: at pass 3 (5 m grid) near_line() answers for |width - 22.86| <= 5 and |width - 45.72| <= 5, area rows only; there is no setting that takes a number of metres

rows.what: made-up squares, true overlap 16 to 22 m (under the 25-yard floor), 4 angles x 4 offsets each (grid-readings.csv)
rows.expect: every spot the grid finds reads 23 to 27 m and is NOT SURE near the 25-yard line; none is shown as very tight

rows.what: true overlap 8 to 15 m
rows.expect: found in 0 of 16 placements at every width: no row at all

rows.what: true overlap 42 to 49 m (either side of the 50-yard line)
rows.expect: every reading on the wrong side of 45.72 m (42-45 m read as 49; 46-49 m read as 45) is NOT SURE near the 50-yard line

rows.what: true overlap 30, 31, 32 m
rows.expect: reads 31 to 37 m: very tight, NOT not-sure (outside one cell of both lines)

rows.what: tests/fixtures/fers-wl3-near-line-rows.csv, water-only rows left out
rows.expect: 226 of 226 rows at the 25-yard line and 154 of 159 at the 50-yard line are NOT SURE (380); with the rule off, 0

rows.what: a river or trail row, and an area row 200 m wide
rows.expect: never touched by the band

rows.what: two made-up overlapping parks named 'Grand Canyon National Park' and 'Kaibab National Forest'; 'Olympic National Park' and 'Olympic National Forest'
rows.expect: decided like any pair (candidate / very tight by width); the words 'two agencies' maps disagree' appear nowhere in the code

rows.what: data/us-key/index.json gets a new 'build' and 'built' while no area was rebuilt (the real case of 19 Nov: build US-44600381160, areas_reused 39, areas_rebuilt 0)
rows.expect: a stamped row whose two parks are unchanged is still copied forward

rows.what: a row with no made_on stamp, through EVERY copy path
rows.expect: never copied; listed in the private folder with the reason; counted in the report; nothing written that says 'not a 2-fer'

rows.what: one park's key entry changes (a record joined or dropped, or its grade)
rows.expect: that park's stamped rows are not copied; a stamped row of another pair in the same area still is

rows.what: the key file cannot be read, or the park is missing from it
rows.expect: not copied, with that reason (fail closed)

rows.what: a 30 m patch 44 m from a listed spot of the same pair, not touching it (both with shapes), store run
rows.expect: its own row, marked fine_only (the Handoff 9 test said NOT its own row under the 100 m rule: that check flips)

rows.what: a patch that touches a listed spot; a 15 m patch; a listed row with no shape
rows.expect: no new row in each case; listed in the private folder with the reason

rows.what: the code
rows.expect: no FINE_GAP_M, no KPC_FERS_FINE_100M, no distance in metres between spots anywhere in the rule

rows.what: a stamped row of a park the run withholds, copied forward
rows.expect: no 'shape', no 'lines'; refs, kind, status, center and size kept; the note is exactly: Possible 2-fer. We are missing an official boundary here: check both official boundary maps before you count it.

rows.what: an UNSTAMPED row of a withheld park
rows.expect: dropped like every old row (owner: 'Drop until re-checked'); nothing replaces it

rows.what: the written public file
rows.expect: holds no coordinate list from the withheld park's row; the write guard, the redaction and the exit-89 refusals are byte for byte main's code

rows.what: .github/fers-rule-scope.json
rows.expect: 2026-11-17-d10-tripwire-not-sure approved with the owner's 19 Nov words; 2026-11-17-thin-shelf kept and marked NOT APPROVED: replaced by the new entry; no THIN_SHELF, no KPC_FERS_SHELF_MIN in the code

rows.what: a public-shelf area whose coverage block says 5 of 50 parks on the shelf
rows.expect: the store run reads it (it is not left on the old path) and the report says '5 of 50 parks on the shelf; 2-fers are measured only between those'

rows.what: a US park whose every record is from a compilation / register / water layer, a Michigan project line or the Mississippi general-area file
rows.expect: its pairs are approximate with SUMMARY_NOTE; a park with one record of its agency's own land is not

rows.what: a park the key grades approximate
rows.expect: its pairs are approximate 2-fers (say which line does it today, or fix it)

rows.what: .github/fers-switches.json missing, broken, or lacking a setting the code asks for
rows.expect: the bot stops with exit 4 and one plain line; it never runs with every rule off

rows.what: an environment variable set against the file
rows.expect: the variable wins, the receipt records the value and 'env', and the run prints one notice

rows.what: a one-character change inside area_spots() with no new scope entry
rows.expect: the math guard test FAILS; with a scope entry that is not 'none' and the fixture updated, it passes

rows.what: the suite run from the checkout root
rows.expect: git status is clean afterwards; data/status/test_fers_final_redact_nov17.json is gone from the repo

rows.what: not-sure-rows-<tag>.json
rows.expect: two runs on the same inputs write the same bytes; no withheld park in it; one row per park per doubt

rows.what: the 17 Nov count of summary-map-only parks
rows.expect: 74 (before the 19 Nov rebuild). Recount; do not test against 74

rows.what: the 17 Nov review's count of passing fine-grid spots that were not counted
rows.expect: 20,749. Not re-measured by the reviewer; do not test against it

rows.what: the 17 Nov count of public files older than the Oct 29-30 key rebuild
rows.expect: 42 files, 1,849 shown rows (from kpc_fers_age.py's own note). Under R-2F4 every row that exists today is old-system data
